html:
The Special Period was the economic crisis that hit Cuba after the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, which had bought its sugar and sold it oil. Cuba lost most of its trade almost overnight.

The economy shrank by about a third. Food, fuel and medicine ran short, blackouts lasted for hours, and Cubans lost weight. People rode bicycles and farmed city plots; organic farming spread for lack of fertiliser.

The government allowed the US dollar, small private businesses and foreign tourism, which became the main earner. In 1994 thousands fled on rafts to Florida in the balsero crisis. The crisis ended the sugar economy and left a lasting gap between Cubans with dollars and those without, under the US embargo and the end of the Soviet Union.
sum: The Special Period was the economic crisis that hit Cuba after the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, which had bought its sugar and sold it oil. Cuba lost most of its trade almost overnight.
